notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 21% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Jordan Kyrou is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Rasmus Sandin is out long term and has missed the last 19 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 54% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 143:34 together.
Zach Hyman is out (impaired vision injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward. Connor McDavid has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 54% of the team’s power-play time in 28 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, down from 30% last season.

story.head: The Oilers need a win
paras: The Oilers are winless in five (0-4-1), and the Capitals (11-12-0) lost 3-2 to Florida on Friday. Going in, the Caps are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (third).

The Capitals have played better than their record (.478) says: their chances are worth about .578, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. The Oilers’ record (.679) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.548), largely thanks to their finishing. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Capitals get their shots through to the net (5th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (28th). They also get some of the league’s best looks (2nd), so the Capitals wait for good looks, but the Oilers settle for hopeful ones. Washington has allowed 3.87 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (most) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and that could do real damage against the Capitals’ penalty kill (27th). Edmonton has scored 3.75 goals a game, the third most in the league.

Alex Tuch (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 23 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead, with seven points in his last five games. Ryan Leonard (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 23 GP) shares it. Connor McDavid (15 G / 45 A / 60 P in 28 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Washington. Leon Draisaitl (24 G / 24 A / 48 P in 28 GP) has a team-high 24 goals, the most in the NHL.
Logan Thompson (8-7-0 / .880 SV% in 17 GS) will likely start for Washington, and Devon Levi (10-4-0 / .889 SV% in 14 GS) for Edmonton.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Dach, Nugent-Hopkins and Kapanen out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Leonard, Protas and Tuch.
